title: Aberrant dopaminergic activity during consolidation causes age-related memory generalization in Drosophila
experiments_summary: The study employed a broad array of genetic, pharmacological, behavioral, and imaging methods in young (3–5 days post-eclosion) and aged (23–25 days at 25°C or 40 days at 18°C) Drosophila. (1) Engram cell identification: UAS-mCD8-GFP; kayak-Gal4/Tubp-Gal80ts flies were subjected to spaced odor/shock conditioning at the Gal80ts restrictive temperature (32°C); GFP-positive c-Fos cells dorsal to mushroom body calyces were counted 24 hours post-training, and odor-dependent reactivation was detected via anti-pERK immunostaining after CS+ or CS− odor re-exposure. (2) Engram functionality: UAS-ChR2::YFP; Kayak-Gal4/Tubp-Gal80ts flies fed all-trans retinal were trained and then given a blue-vs.-green light choice to assess whether optogenetic activation of engram cells drove avoidance behavior. (3) Behavioral generalization assays: Flies underwent spaced paired training, CS+-only training, odor-alone (mock) training, or unpaired training protocols; odor avoidance indices (AI) were measured by presenting individual odors (CS+, CS−, novel odors) versus air in a T-maze, and standard performance indices (PI) comparing CS+ vs. CS− were computed. Controls included radish (rsh1) ARM mutants and massed training. (4) Glial glutamate transporter manipulation: Eaat1 was acutely knocked down in glia of young flies using an RU486-inducible glial geneswitch driver; aged flies were fed NMDA receptor antagonists memantine or MK801 after training, and engram reactivation was re-examined via anti-pERK staining. (5) Klg cell-type screen: klg RNAi was expressed in ellipsoid bodies, mushroom bodies, astrocyte-glia, glutamatergic neurons, all dopaminergic neurons (TH-Gal4), PPL1 dopaminergic neurons (MB060B), and PAM cluster neurons, and LTM was assayed. (6) Extracellular glutamate imaging: iGluSnFR was expressed in MB060B-labeled PPL1 neurons; fluorescence was recorded 3 hours after spaced training in young and aged flies with or without the glutamate transporter blocker UCPH-101. (7) PPL1 neuronal activity measurements: (a) Bioluminescence assay—flies expressing Lolap-luciferase in PPL1 neurons were fed D-luciferin and luminescence was recorded every 16 minutes for 20 hours post-training; glutamate receptor inhibitors riluzole and memantine were used to probe the source of increased activity. (b) Calcium imaging—GCaMP3 expressed in MB060B neurons was imaged at 4 Hz for 4 min 16 s in naïve animals and 3 hours post-training; Fourier power spectra were computed; MK801 and UCPH-101 were applied pharmacologically. (c) Phospho-S6 immunostaining—anti-phospho-S6 and anti-TH antibodies were used on paraffin sections to detect activity-dependent S6 phosphorylation in TH+ neurons after spaced vs. massed training, and after ectopic glial Eaat1 expression. (8) PPL1 DREADD manipulations: MB060B>hM4Di (inhibitory) or MB060B>hM1Dq (excitatory) flies were fed CNO after training; LTM and generalization were assessed in young and aged flies. (9) NMDAR manipulations on PPL1 neurons: RNAi knockdown of NR1 in MB060B neurons was performed; wild-type NR1 and a constitutively active Mg2+-block mutant (NR1 N631Q) were overexpressed; LTM and generalization were measured. Extracellular ion concentrations (Mg2+, Ca2+, K+, Na+) were measured in head hemolymph using double-barreled ion-sensitive microelectrodes. (10) Dopamine receptor knockdown in engram cells: Dop1R1, Dop1R2, Dop2R, and DopEcR RNAi lines were expressed under kayak-Gal4/Tub-Gal80ts control in engram cells during training; LTM and generalization were measured in young and aged flies. Sulpiride (Dop2R antagonist) was fed to aged flies during consolidation. (11) α2sc MBON calcium imaging: LexAop-GCaMP6f driven by R34B02-lexA (MBON-α2sc) was imaged in vivo 20–24 hours post-training; flies were sequentially exposed to CS+, CS−, and novel odors; log10 ratios of CS+ to other odor responses were computed. Memantine feeding, PPL1-DREADD inhibition, and dopamine synthesis blockade with 3-iodotyrosine (3IY) were each tested for restoration of odor-differential responses in aged flies. All statistical analyses used Student's t-test or ANOVA with post-hoc tests via GraphPad Prism.
